# theirs: hw_eval.cuh holtwinters_eval_gpu_shared_kernel (:96-156) and hw_optim.cuh holtwinters_optim_gpu_shared_kernel (:588-709)

# theirs: hw_decompose.cuh batched_ls's cuSOLVER geqrf/orgqr, its two bufferSize queries, cuBLAS gemm, and RinvKernel (:114-127)
why / where it would go: R^-1 Q^T IS pinv([1, t]) and is a function of trend_len ALONE, not of any series. Their route to it runs through two CLOSED libraries whose float32 output is neither readable nor bit-reproducible across GPU models. Ours writes the same matrix on the host in float64 from the closed form and casts. Their DATA-TOUCHING kernel is ported unchanged. Priced: our R1Qt is not expected to be their bits in the last places, and this is one of the two spots the lane is not cuML's numbers

status: PORTED BUT NOT CALLED on the launch path
why / where it would go: get_num_blocks mirrors the cap faithfully in hw_utils.mojo, but every kernel launcher here computes (n + tpb - 1) // tpb directly and does NOT cap. # theirs: hw_optim.cuh the cuml#888 line-search bug (:485-508)
why / where it would go: when the line search hits its iteration limit, the LAST nx is stored rather than the nx that minimised loss. It is flagged in their own comment (:346-349) and issue. It is a genuine defect, but unlike DEVIATION 697 it is DETERMINISTIC and vendor-independent: the same inputs give the same wrong answer on every GPU, which is what this lane certifies. Fixing it would change the fitted parameters away from cuML's for no identity gain. Recorded here so the choice is visible rather than silent

why / where it would go: unlike DEVIATION 662's route this is their arithmetic on a non-degenerate input, it terminates deterministically through the same NaN -> bound_device -> +0.0 chain on every vendor, and the card hashes its NaNs through DEVIATION 661's single payload.
